newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's hard left to vote "no' to Albania force.
newsitem.headline: Italy's hard left to vote "no' to Albania force.

text.p: Italy's hard left Communist Refoundation party, a key parliamentary ally of Prime Minister Romano Prodi, confirmed on Monday that it would vote against sending an Italian-led multinational security force to Albania.

A party statement said Refoundation's leadership had invited its members of parliament to vote "no' to the mission in votes due this week, a step that will split Prodi's parliamentary majority on a major policy issue for the first time.
"The leadership decided unanimously to confirm our position," party leader Fausto Bertinotti told reporters.

He reaffirmed the party's line that the risks of the mission were too great to Italian soldiers, who will account for some 2,000 of the up to 6,000 troops, and that the United Nations should send peacekeepers.

The force, the first of its kind to be led by Italy, will protect and assist the delivery of aid to the Balkan state, rocked by lawlessness and armed anarchy. It is due to deploy in the week from April 14.
Prodi is certain of victory when the two houses of parliament hold votes on the force on Tuesday and Wednesday because of backing for the deployment from the main opposition.
But the split with Refoundation has confronted Prodi with his toughest political challenge in 11 months of office.
Refoundation is not part of the government but ensures its majority in the lower house of parliament, where it holds the balance of power.
Angry coalition parties have questioned whether the uneasy alliance with Refoundation can survive the rift and talked of the possibility of an early general election or minority government.
